memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If, however, they cannot afford two doves or two young pigeons, they are to bring as an offering for their sin a tenth of an ephah of the finest flour for a sin offering. They must not put olive oil or incense on it, because it is a sin offering.'" - Lev 5:11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God descends one final step. Cannot afford even two birds? Bring a small measure of flour — about two litres.

This is remarkable. For the first and only time, a sin offering involves no blood at all. God made a way for the destitute person to be forgiven.

Does that contradict Hebrews 9:22, that without blood there is no forgiveness? No — and here is why. The flour was burned on an altar that was already soaked in blood, in a system entirely built on substitution. The poor man's flour was accepted because of blood, even though it was not his own blood offering. He was carried by the sacrifices of others.

That is a profound picture. The poorest Israelite in the nation was forgiven on the strength of a sacrifice he could not provide.

And note what he must not add: no oil, no incense. Those belonged to the grain offering of thanksgiving. This is not a celebration. God does not let the poor man's offering pretend to be something festive. The occasion is still sin, and it is treated with appropriate gravity.

God's kindness does not require pretending. He meets us honestly, exactly where we are.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I believe God has made a way for me even when I have nothing to bring?
2. Am I resting on a sacrifice I could never have provided myself?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I have nothing to offer that could pay for my sin. Thank You that You provided what I could not, and that Your welcome reaches even the empty-handed. Amen.
